yt_description:
Hank's 2007 G 500 has three locking differentials: front, center and rear. Lock all three and every wheel gets driven. The catch: on a 20-year-old G, lockers that were never used often don't work. The usual fix is finding a vacuum leak, then bleeding the hydraulic lines.

How to check the lockers, and every G 500 year: https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/g500/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=hook-test

Filmed on Hank's own truck. Voiceover is AI-generated.
yt_comment: Thanks for watching! If you're test-driving a W463, engage each locker in turn and make sure the dash light comes on. Lockers that won't engage are usually a vacuum problem: confirm vacuum at the transfer-case hose, then work back through the pump, manifold and switchover valves. One owner's 2005 G 500 fault was a split plastic connector under the brake booster. Full guide: https://boxytrucks.com/repairs/g-class/w463/lockers-won-t-engage-find-the-vacuum-leak/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=comment Do yours all work?
